topic: What happens if you jump at the last second in a falling elevator?
title: Falling Elevator
idea: Jumping at the last second barely helps; the real safety is the ropes and brakes, and the longest elevator fall survived was luck and physics.
hook: The cable just snapped. You're dropping down the shaft.

beats.line: You plan to jump. But your best jump is about seven miles an hour.
beats.see: Hero crouches inside the falling car, floor lights streaking past; a small speed tag '7 MPH' pops above his head on 'seven'.

beats.line: From one hundred sixty five feet, you hit at seventy two miles an hour.
beats.see: Side cutaway of the shaft with a height ruler '165 FT'; the car rushes down, speedometer needle swings to 72 on 'seventy two'.

beats.line: Jump perfectly. Guess your new speed.
beats.see: Freeze frame mid jump; big guess dial with a blinking '?' and a 3 second countdown starting on 'Guess'.

beats.line: Sixty five. Barely better, and you can't time it.
beats.see: Dial drops only from 72 to 65 on 'Sixty five'; hero lands, the jump clock beside him spins wildly on 'time'.

beats.line: Back up the shaft. Elevators hang on several steel ropes.
beats.see: Camera whooshes up the shaft on 'Back'; above the car, a bundle of thick paper ropes fans out, a counter ticks each rope on 'several'.

beats.line: Plus automatic brakes built to stop a fall.
beats.see: Brake jaws on the rails snap shut on 'brakes', sparks fly, the car stops dead on 'stop'.

beats.line: Betty Lou Oliver fell seventy five floors in the Empire State Building.
beats.see: Paper Empire State Building, a 1945 bomber silhouette hits the tower, a floor counter runs down from 75 on 'seventy five'.

beats.line: Trapped air and coiled cables cushioned her. She broke her back, but lived.
beats.see: Cutaway of the shaft bottom: air puffs swell under the car on 'air', a coiled cable heap squashes like a spring on 'cables'; stamp SURVIVED on 'lived'.

end.line: When the cable snaps, forget the jump. Remember Betty.
end.see: Cable twangs and snaps on 'snaps' (loops into hook), the jump icon gets crossed out on 'forget', Betty's cutout portrait with a record ribbon on 'Betty'.

description: The cable snaps and you jump at the last second. Here is how much that actually helps.

facts.claim: Best human jump is about 7 mph; from 165 ft impact drops only from about 72 to 65 mph; you cannot time the jump.
Elevators hang on several steel ropes and have automatic safety brakes.
facts.source: Industry sources per FACTS file (Otis safety brake, 1854) [snippet, no number used]

facts.claim: Betty Lou Oliver survived a 75-storey elevator fall in the Empire State Building (28 July 1945, plane crash cut the cables).
Air trapped in the shaft and coiled cables cushioned the car; she broke her back, neck and pelvis and survived.

notes: Guess answer: 65 (from 72). Honest framing: no trick is offered; 'barely better' not 'does nothing'. Lying flat deliberately left out. 'Brakes built to stop a fall' rests on snippet-level industry sources, no statistic given. The 1945 plane in the 'see' is visual only (in Guinness/Archives). Hook uses 'cable' singular as a movie trope; the script then corrects it with 'several steel ropes'.
